title: Pre-Analysis — Extension of the Solid State Lighting Conversion to the Remaining Cabins

ata.title: Passenger Compartment Lighting — Ceiling and Wall Wash Lights

abstract: Closed pre-analysis of a proposed revision bringing the two excluded aircraft and the upper deck lobby into the solid state ceiling and wall wash lighting conversion, with the sidewall interface as the main open question.

sections.objective: Determine whether the two aircraft excluded from the original conversion and the upper deck lobby can be brought onto the solid state standard under the existing modification rather than through a new one, and identify what the extension touches in the sidewall interface, in the published bulletins and in the two cabin changes that are currently in work on the same panels. The order came from the cabin systems office after both excluded operators asked for the conversion at their next cabin refresh.
sections.findings_summary: Four items were confirmed and none of them blocked the extension. The larger part of the lobby work is already covered by the second lighting bulletin, which was written for the extended premium lobby layout and reaches further aft than the cabin systems office believed; the extension therefore adds less than it appeared to. The window pane change now in work takes the same sidewall panel interface at two of the three strip stations, and the two have to agree a single panel cutout. The parts list gains the lobby strip lengths. The fourth item is the seat power uprating, which shares nothing with this document and depends on the load reduction this conversion delivers.
sections.next_steps: The extension was cleared to proceed as a revision of the existing modification rather than as a new change. The lobby scope was cut back to what the second bulletin does not already cover. A single sidewall panel cutout was agreed with the window design office and recorded as a shared interface item, with the lighting conversion publishing the profile because it freezes first. The load reduction figure was restated in the effects text so that the seat power work can cite it.

similarity_seeds: cabin lighting conversion in a premium lobby area
sidewall panel interface shared by lighting and window work

tasks.title: Establish what the two lighting bulletins already cover
Compare the sidewall panel interface against the cabin work in progress
Restate the cabin load reduction for the extended scope

expected_findings.rationale: The second lighting bulletin was written for the extended premium lobby layout and reaches further aft than the request assumed. Most of the proposed lobby work is already accomplishable today on the aircraft concerned, and the extension would duplicate it.
expected_findings.resolution: Cut the lobby scope back to what the bulletin does not cover and state the boundary by frame station in the revision.

expected_findings.rationale: The window pane assembly change takes the same sidewall panel interface at two of the three strip stations, and each change assumes its own panel cutout. Whichever is embodied second would have to cut a panel that the first already trimmed.
expected_findings.resolution: Agree one sidewall panel cutout as a shared interface item; the lighting conversion publishes the profile because it freezes first.

evidence.similarity_note: The figure and the modification describe the same lighting channel assembly and name the strip, the diffuser and the channel end cap identically.

expected_findings.rationale: The lobby strips are a different length from every item currently in the figure and cannot be carried as alternates of the cabin strips, because the diffuser is cut to the same length and the two would be ordered interchangeably.
expected_findings.resolution: Add the lobby lengths as their own items with a zone effectivity and mark the cabin items as not applicable in the lobby.

evidence.similarity_note: Nothing in common but the busbar. One document reduces cabin lighting demand and says so only in its effects text; the other adds seat power demand and says so only in its own. No shared part number, FIN, zone or chapter, and neither cites the other.

expected_findings.rationale: The seat power uprating in pre-analysis closes its load budget only on an aircraft that has taken this conversion. Extending the conversion to the two excluded aircraft therefore also unblocks the seat work on them, which is worth stating in both documents.
expected_findings.resolution: Restate the load reduction figure in the effects text so the seat power candidate can cite it as a precondition.

expected_non_findings.reason: Shares two cabin zones and is retrieved by any sidewall search, and its subject even sounds adjacent since it repairs the window frame surround. It is a structural blend out and strap repair that stops at the frame; it touches no panel cutout and no lighting channel.

type_data.conclusion: Issued 2026-06-05. The extension proceeds as a revision, with the lobby scope reduced and a single sidewall cutout agreed with the window design office.
